headline: Oracle has again asked US federal regulators to speed up approval of a 17.8-mile natural gas pipeline needed to power its Project Jupiter data center campus in New Mexico.
score_reason: Fresh letter and concrete delay figures from Bloomberg; a request, not a decision.
importance_line: Residents and regulators in New Mexico are caught between promised jobs and environmental concerns, Oracle's large AI project depends on a pipeline it does not control, and trucking in gas, which Oracle is considering, would likely cover only the start-up phase.
summary: Bloomberg reports that Oracle has renewed its request that the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) approve as quickly as possible the 17.8-mile gas pipeline for its Project Jupiter data center campus in New Mexico, with Josh Pitcock, its senior vice president of government affairs, writing in a letter on Tuesday: "Time remains of the essence." The pipeline, which would feed Bloom Energy fuel cells (devices that make electricity directly from gas) at the site, has already slipped to February 2027 from 15 August, and New Mexico's attorney general, Raúl Torrez, says FERC must either revise its environmental assessment or carry out a full environmental impact study.
notes: Bloomberg original blocked; Bloomberg text read on Yahoo Finance; cross-checked with Investing.com.
